summary: Material change since the morning snapshot is in global energy transmission rather than official macro releases. Reuters reported Saudi Arabia is now offering additional crude to Asian buyers via ship-to-ship loading off Sohar, Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz, partially mitigating disruption from the damaged East-West Pipeline and halted Yanbu loadings. Separately, Reuters reported Russia decided to extend diesel-export restrictions for producers through end-October, increasing persistence of the refined-product shock. Oil prices eased on September 16 as Saudi alternative routing and higher U.S. inventories reduced immediate crude-scarcity fears, while diesel remained exceptionally tight. The Federal Reserve decision was still pending at this snapshot; no decision is pre-assumed.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Saudi alternative routing is a partial de-escalation for crude availability, but persistent Russian diesel restrictions keep freight and refined-product inflation risk elevated. Airlines and energy-intensive manufacturers remain exposed to high fuel costs; shipping has mixed volume/rerouting and bunker-cost effects; long-duration technology remains sensitive to oil-driven inflation and bond yields.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market observations and semantic scores are research evidence only.

key_drivers.name: Saudi alternative export routing via Oman
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Saudi Arabia offered additional Arab Light, Medium and Heavy crude to Asian term buyers via ship-to-ship loading off Sohar, Oman, outside Hormuz. Gulf loadings at Ras Tanura and Juaymah were reported near 4 million bpd.
key_drivers.interpretation: This is an observed mitigation channel that reduces complete-export-loss risk, but does not restore Yanbu or the East-West Pipeline and does not eliminate Hormuz/Red Sea logistics risk.

key_drivers.name: Russia extends diesel export restrictions
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Russia decided to extend diesel-export restrictions for producers through the end of October.
key_drivers.interpretation: This raises persistence of the refined-product shock and supports diesel cracks, freight costs and energy-inflation risk even if crude scarcity eases.

key_drivers.name: Fed and Taiwan central-bank event risk
key_drivers.observed: The official Fed decision was still pending at this snapshot; Taiwan's central-bank decision is due September 17.
key_drivers.interpretation: Policy-event risk remains high because energy inflation and elevated yields constrain easing and increase the probability of tighter policy.

key_risks: Saudi alternative routing proves insufficient or itself encounters security/logistics constraints.
Yanbu and East-West Pipeline outages persist longer than expected.
Russian diesel-export restrictions through end-October sustain global freight and refined-product inflation.
Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb security risks remain unresolved despite alternative routing.
Fed and Taiwan central-bank decisions create immediate policy-event risk.
VIX, copper, USD/TWD and exact newer official Treasury closes remain stale in this semantic snapshot.
